title: fw-conntrack-saturation-runbook-draft
summary: Draft runbook and incident notes for a pattern we've seen where customer-managed firewalls / NAT devices saturate connection-tracking (conntrack) and cause intermittent loss of control-plane reachability for on-prem / VPC private deployments. This doc captures detection, immediate mitigations used on call, root cause analysis, and recommended long-term fixes and alerts.
impact: For affected clusters (customer A, private deployment), the Redwood agent lost control-plane connectivity intermittently for ~2.5 hours which caused failed heartbeats, temporary inability to deploy new model versions, and increased request latency for routed traffic. No data leakage was observed. Impact classification: P2 (degraded availability for a customer).
incident_description: On 2026-02-13 22:17 UTC customer A reported service flakiness in their private deployment. On-call observed repeated drops in agent->control-plane websocket connections and transient 502/504 errors on control-plane API calls. The pattern correlated with spikes in short-lived outbound connections from agents and a spike on the customer's firewall NAT/conntrack table. The customer's perimeter device (vendor: GenericStatefulFW) had conntrack table limits set conservatively and aggressive state timeouts. During a downstream batch job run (customer internal analytics), the number of concurrent ephemeral sessions increased >10x which filled the conntrack table and prevented new connections from establishing.
timeline:
- 2026-02-13 22:10 UTC: Customer opens support channel reporting intermittent control-plane failures.
- 2026-02-13 22:15 UTC: On-call (Ethan) begins investigating logs; sees agent connection retries and backoff; control-plane telemetry shows heartbeat failures.
- 2026-02-13 22:22 UTC: Correlate with customer network team — they report spike at 22:18 UTC on their NAT device.
- 2026-02-13 22:28 UTC: Customer runs 'conntrack -S' and reports 100% usage of nf_conntrack (table size 65536).
- 2026-02-13 22:35 UTC: Mitigation 1: Customer increases nf_conntrack_max to 262144 and rebalances state timeouts; partial recovery in 4 minutes.
- 2026-02-13 22:45 UTC: Mitigation 2: We enable persistent keepalive on agent connections and push an agent config change to reuse HTTP connections for internal control-plane calls; reduces churn.
- 2026-02-13 23:05 UTC: Stability returns for normal traffic patterns; full recovery by 23:20 UTC.
- 2026-02-14: Post-incident calls to review root cause and next steps.
observations_and_diagnostics:
- Agent logs: repeated TCP connection resets and websocket reconnects; stack traces showed short-lived sessions being created for roster/status calls.
- Customer FW: conntrack table reached max (nf_conntrack_max = 65536). Metrics: conntrack_inuse=65536, conntrack_failed_alloc=high.
- tcpdump on edge: large burst of SYN/SYN-ACK pairs from internal host pool during analytics job.
- Control-plane logs: increase in 502/504 when ephemeral connections failed to complete handshake.
- No kernel-level OOMs or node resource issues observed on Redwood side.
root_cause: Primary: Connection-tracking table saturation on customer-managed NAT/firewall due to a burst of short-lived outbound connections from customer jobs. Secondary contributors: default/low nf_conntrack_max and state timeouts on the firewall; agent behavior creating many ephemeral connections instead of reusing persistent connections for control-plane RPCs in some code paths. Also lacking proactive alerting on conntrack usage at >=80%.
immediate_mitigation:
- Work with customer network team to increase nf_conntrack_max to a safe headroom (temporary change to 262144) and adjust per-protocol timeouts.
- Push agent config to enable persistent HTTP keepalives and reduce per-request connection churn.
- Ask customer to throttle the burst workload where possible and schedule heavy analytics outside peak windows.
- Add temporary rate-limiter on our API gateway for this customer's control-plane traffic to reduce connection pressure while fixing agent behaviour.
runbook_draft:
Purpose: Provide on-call steps to detect and mitigate conntrack saturation issues affecting control-plane reachability for private/VPC deployments.
Prereqs: SSH or equivalent access to customer perimeter device (or their network team contact), shell access on affected agent hosts, ability to push agent config changes via our deployment tooling.
Detection:
  - Alert: control-plane-heartbeat-missed > 3x in 5min AND repeated agent reconnects.
  - Verify with: netstat/ss summary, control-plane logs, agent logs.
Quick checks (commands):
  - sudo conntrack -S || sudo conntrack -L | wc -l  (conntrack inuse)
  - sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max
  - ss -s (socket stats)
  - sudo cat /proc/net/nf_conntrack | wc -l  (if conntrack tool not present)
  - sudo iptables -nvL --line-numbers (check NAT rules)
  - sudo tcpdump -ni <edge-if> 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn) != 0' and watch burst behavior
Immediate steps to mitigate (ordered):
  1) Ask customer to temporarily pause or stagger the high-volume job.
  2) If allowed, ask customer to increase nf_conntrack_max (example: sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144) and persist in /etc/sysctl.d/99-local.conf.
  3) Suggest lowering conntrack timeout for specific protocols (reduce default TCP/UDP timeout) on firewall where safe.
  4) Deploy agent config patch to enable keepalive and HTTP connection reuse; roll to affected hosts.
  5) If the device supports it, enable connection tracking hashsize tuning and connection tracking offload to hardware.
  6) Monitor for drop in conntrack_failed_allocs and restoration of control-plane heartbeats.
Post-Mitigation Checklist:
  - Confirm control-plane heartbeats stable for 30min.
  - Verify no increased errors in API gateway logs.
  - Ask customer to provide planned schedule for heavy jobs and document network limits.
action_items: Implement agent-side persistent connection default for control-plane RPCs (engineering ticket SRE-4123)
Add proactive alert: conntrack_inuse >= 80% (integrated when we have customer networking metrics)
Create KB for customer network teams outlining recommended nf_conntrack sizing guidance
Add runbook snippet in Redwood Console 'Private Deployments -> Network Troubleshooting' and link to this doc
Test agent changes in staging with synthetic high-connection churn to validate behavior
Follow-up meeting with customer network team to discuss long-term firewall tuning and monitoring
postmortem_notes:
Learnings: We need earlier visibility into customer-managed NAT state for private deployments. Where we can't get metric streams, we should have explicit pre-deploy checks and customer onboarding guidance documenting NAT/conntrack expectations. The agent should avoid creating per-request new TCP connections to control-plane; reusing connections significantly reduces pressure on stateful devices. Also add an SLA-runbook about scheduled heavy jobs.
Risk: Some customer firewalls are managed via change control and can't be tuned quickly; we must have mitigations that don't rely on immediate FW changes (agent hardening, gateway rate-limits).
